Looking at the parameters by eye, the hidden-layer biases stand out. Most of `b1` ranges from about -0.45 to 0.65, but the first four entries are all tiny positive values that look planted rather than trained:

| b1 index | value | ×1000 | letter (A=1) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.018 | 18 | R |
| 1 | 0.009 | 9 | I |
| 2 | 0.019 | 19 | S |
| 3 | 0.001 | 1 | A |

Everything else in the network reads like ordinary trained features. For example, W1 rows 27, 29 and 30 are clean line detectors for the top row, right column and bottom row, with positive weights on the mover's cells and negative weights on the opponent's. W2 and b2 show no clean numeric pattern. The four leading biases, all in the 1 to 26 range when scaled by 1000 and sitting at the very start of the vector, are the one spot that reads as a deliberate edit.
